summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is retained: dementia (Alzheimer disease and vascular dementia) trials with cognitive and daily-function findings and high risk of bias; no healthy-adult focus or cognition benefit is shown. Re-extracted from the PMC full texts. 24086396 (PMC3781107): 20 RCTs, 1,823 Alzheimer patients, 0.2-0.8 mg/day for 8-36 weeks; MMSE, HDS, WMS and ADL favoured huperzine A at 8-16 weeks (moderate GRADE), no trial measured quality of life, and most trials were at moderate or poor methodological quality. 24639880 (PMC3930088): 8 AD trials and 2 vascular-dementia trials, 100-500 μg/day; MMSE WMD 2.79 and ADL -4.84 in AD, with heterogeneity and suspected publication bias. The U.S. phase II RCT (21502597) missed its primary ADAS-Cog endpoint at 200 μg twice daily. These are dementia populations, so per Dr. Pham's rulings there is no healthy-adult focus, cognition or longevity credit; the record is reference-only with approved no-credit contexts that keep their true directions.

read.finding: 2022 umbrella review (16 reviews, 149 studies): AChE inhibitors, huperzine A among them, appeared beneficial for cognition, global performance and ADL in Alzheimer's disease.

read.title: Pharmacological treatments for vascular dementia: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
read.finding: 2024 NMA, 194 RCTs in vascular dementia: huperzine A ranked second for MMSE and first for ADL among 21 drugs.

read.title: Huperzine A for the treatment of cognitive, mood, and functional deficits after moderate and severe TBI (HUP-TBI): results of a Phase II randomized controlled pilot study: implications for understanding the placebo effect.
read.finding: 2020 phase II RCT in moderate-severe TBI, 12 weeks: no difference vs placebo in CVLT-II memory; placebo-group improvement.

freshness_search.conclusion: confirms: newer syntheses support huperzine A only within Alzheimer's and vascular dementia. The one newer non-dementia RCT (TBI) was null, and no trial tests healthy adults. No healthy-adult focus or longevity credit.
